no_invented_permissions.note: Every norm predicate is a duty of an instance of Claude (first argument), so no rule or completion says anything about a party the source does not name, and no predicate says what is permitted. The completion of every predicate is deny, which for a duty means only “not required”. The nine prohibitions are written as duties to avoid the act, so a case the defeasible reading lifts (its exception applies) reads “not required to avoid”, the meaning of a lifted duty, and not “not permitted”, which the source does not say. Limitation that remains: the language has no third outcome “unspecified”, so “not required” is still a completion that the source never states.

in_the_translation_itself.meaning: The translation has norm and soft-norm units and one fenced clause. A discourse document must record every slot of a unit that has meaning; the translation's reading-set units have unrecorded slots, and the spec (docs/spec/discourse.md 11) says norm and soft-norm composition is not implemented. So the upgrade cannot enter the main document: u0214.s02 stays UNFORMALISED (other:discourse) there, and only the norms-free companion probe is admitted.
